confirmed.statement: (a) The document says assignment was random. Section 4.1 says 'Participants were randomly assigned to one condition and completed a user persona creation task with AI assistance structured according to their assigned pattern.' The same page adds 'Random assignment employed sequential balancing to ensure approximately equal group sizes across conditions.' Figure 2 has a box labeled 'Random Assignment to 4 Conditions'. The form's assignment quote is verbatim and its locator is right.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 9 (journal p. 8), Section 4.1; PDF p. 10 (journal p. 9), Figure 2

confirmed.statement: The mechanism is thin. The paper never says what 'sequential balancing' is. A rotation by arrival order would be systematic, not random, but the paper calls it random assignment. A full-text search finds no other wording on allocation (no 'allocat', 'self-select', 'wave', 'batch', or 'pilot'). The form already flags this in open_questions.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 9, Section 4.1; full text, PDF pp. 1-32

confirmed.statement: Design is between-subjects with individual assignment. Section 4.1 says 'We conducted a between-subjects experiment with four conditions', and Section 6.1 says 'participants in our study used a single pattern throughout'. So unit = individual and structure = between are right, and check (e) on the order of conditions does not apply.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 9, Section 4.1; PDF p. 2, Abstract ('between-subjects experiment (N = 244)'); PDF p. 24 (journal p. 23), Section 6.1

confirmed.statement: (b) What was assigned is AI help on the participant's own artifact, not a change in whose output is rated. Each participant wrote a persona and scenario in a rich text editor, and 'All conditions provided access to a rich text editor for creating the persona and scenario, with conditions differing in how AI assistance was structured.' The judges rated each participant's own persona. This matches what_was_assigned.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 9, Section 4.1; PDF pp. 10-11, Section 4.3 (task brief); PDF p. 11, Section 4.4; PDF p. 12, Section 4.5

confirmed.statement: (c) The tool is generative AI. Every condition used 'identical underlying AI capabilities (Gemini 2.5 Flash-Lite (preview release 09/2025), accessed through OpenRouter as google/gemini-2.5-flash-lite-preview-09–2025, with condition-specific system prompts'. Appendix A repeats the model and prints each prompt. ai_tool.name_model is right.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 11 (journal p. 10), Section 4.4; PDF pp. 30-31 (journal pp. 29-30), Appendix A

confirmed.statement: (d) The comparison arm is another AI configuration. All four conditions listed in Section 4.1 use the AI, and no condition works without it. So arms[].ai = generative_ai for all four, 'there is no no-AI arm', and comparison_type = ai_design are right.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 9, Section 4.1; PDF p. 11, Section 4.4

confirmed.statement: The four arm descriptions match the PDF. HLE: a dropdown with the five listed options, output 'in a separate panel', and participants 'required to manually integrate any AI suggestions'. ALP: five AI-generated cards, then free chat in which the AI 'could see the participant’s current work and discuss it but could not make direct changes', and a prompt saying 'Your role is ONLY to help them elaborate and develop THIS SPECIFIC proposal'. IC: a 'Get Feedback' button, three sections of 2-3 points, no limit on cycles, and the AI 'does not produce drafts'. FD: a split-pane chat in which the AI could view but not edit the workspace, and a prompt saying 'Be constructively critical'. The form's 'In all arms only the participant could write in the workspace' holds for all four.
confirmed.locator: PDF pp. 11-12 (journal pp. 10-11), Sections 4.4.1-4.4.4; PDF p. 7 (journal p. 6), Section 3.3; PDF pp. 30-31, Appendix A

confirmed.statement: Counts match. Section 4.2 says 'A total of 275 participants were initially assigned to one of four human–AI interaction patterns. After applying the predefined data quality criteria, 31 participants were excluded, resulting in a final sample of 244 participants.' Table 1 and Figure 2 give HLE 60, ALP 62, IC 61, FD 61, which sum to 244. No per-arm count at assignment is printed, so arms[].n_randomized = null is right.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 9, Section 4.2; PDF p. 10, Table 1 and Figure 2

confirmed.statement: Figure 2 conflicts with the text on when assignment happened. The figure draws 'Final Sample N=244' before 'Random Assignment to 4 Conditions', with the analyzed arm sizes. The text says 275 were assigned and 31 were excluded after that. Two exclusion rules use in-task logs ('fewer than 3 logged interactions or completed the experiment in less than 3 minutes'), so they can only apply after assignment. The form follows the text (n_randomized = 275) and flags the conflict. Under the text's order, arms of 68 or 69 at assignment and 60 to 62 analyzed imply 6 to 9 exclusions per arm (this check's arithmetic; the paper prints no exclusions by arm). Either order leaves random assignment in place.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 10, Figure 2; PDF p. 9, Section 4.2

confirmed.statement: Preregistration rests on one phrase. Section 4.2 says 'Substantial exclusions were applied based on pre-registered quality criteria', and the next paragraph calls the same criteria 'predefined'. No registry, link, preregistered hypothesis, or preregistered outcome appears. preregistered = yes, with that limit stated in prereg_locator, matches the text.

The paper contradicts itself once on IC, and the form takes the right side. Section 5.2.2 says 'IC positions the AI as a generator of drafts subject to human evaluation'. Section 3.3 says the AI 'does not produce drafts', Section 4.4.3 describes feedback only, and the IC system prompt asks only for strengths, areas for improvement, and recommendations. The form's IC description follows the operational sections and the prompt.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 18 (journal p. 17), Section 5.2.2; PDF p. 7, Section 3.3; PDF p. 12, Section 4.4.3; PDF pp. 30-31, Appendix A

confirmed.statement: FD is not a plain chatbot. Its system prompt included '[Evaluation rubric summary provided for context]' and 'YOUR ROLE: Guide the user toward creating high-quality work that meets these criteria.' Section 3.5 says 'In IC and FD, the AI primarily evaluates content'. The form's FD description mentions the critical prompt but not the rubric. The form already says no arm is a plain default. This bears on which arm serves as the reference in ai_design contrasts, not on criterion 1.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 31 (journal p. 30), Appendix A; PDF p. 7 (journal p. 6), Section 3.5

confirmed.statement: ALP cards may have carried more AI content than the form says. Section 4.4.2 says 'Each card contained a persona name and demographic sketch', and the form repeats this. The generation prompt also asked for a primary motivation, one key frustration, and 'a brief scenario suggestion (2–3 sentences)'. The paper does not say whether the cards showed those parts. The form's wording is supported by Section 4.4.2. This matters for reading the ALP scenario results, not for eligibility.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 11, Section 4.4.2; PDF p. 30 (journal p. 29), Appendix A

summary: The PDF supports every part of the assignment, arms, and ai_tool coding: Section 4.1 says participants 'were randomly assigned to one condition' with 'sequential balancing', each of the four between-subjects arms gave the participant a differently configured Gemini 2.5 Flash-Lite assistant for their own persona and scenario, no arm lacks AI, and 275 were assigned and 244 analyzed (HLE 60, ALP 62, IC 61, FD 61) (PDF pp. 9-11). The caveats leave criterion 1 intact: the paper never describes the balancing procedure, Figure 2 draws assignment after the 244-person final sample while the text excludes 31 people after assignment, and free dialogue, the form's reference arm, ran a rubric-primed critical prompt rather than a plain chatbot (PDF pp. 9-10, 31).
